detailZh: 刘易斯·汉密尔顿（汉密尔顿）在意大利大奖赛前分享了自己对成为首位在意大利夺冠的黑人法拉利车手的可能性的看法
刘易斯·汉密尔顿本周末将在蒙扎寻求他在意大利为法拉利取得的首场胜利；汉密尔顿希望法拉利的引擎升级能提升他的获胜机会；请于上午11:30和下午3点观看意大利大奖赛周五练习赛的直播，天空体育 F1将进行实况转播
刘易斯·汉密尔顿乘坐一辆罕见的法拉利F40抵达意大利大奖赛，并透露这辆车的引擎编号与他的赛车号码相同。
刘易斯·汉密尔顿表示，在本周末的意大利大奖赛之前，他一直在考虑成为法拉利车队首位赢得主场赛事的黑人F1车手这一潜在成就的重大意义。
这位七届世界冠军在红色的第二个赛季中表现出明显进步，今年6月在巴塞罗那为车队赢得首场大奖赛胜利，帮助他保持争冠希望，目前他落后梅赛德斯的安东内利 59分，还剩11轮比赛。
汉密尔顿在蒙扎夺冠的希望得到了提振，因为Antonelli因超出引擎部件配额将受罚，从发车末位起步。

当被问及潜在的第107场职业大奖赛胜利对他意味着什么时，汉密尔顿说：“进入这个周末之前我真的思考过，我反复琢磨，只是想到我要来参加这场大奖赛这一概念的巨大意义，比如我甚至不知道我已经和迈克尔[舒马赫]在[蒙扎五胜]上持平了。”
法拉利车队的刘易斯·汉密尔顿在巴塞罗那-加泰罗尼亚大奖赛上取得了他身穿红色战袍的首场胜利。
“但我的前方还有第一次，意思是说，如果我有可能获胜，那将进入全新的领域。
“穿着法拉利的战袍首次在蒙扎获胜——我曾目睹夏尔（勒克莱尔）在2019年做到过，当时我和他一起登上了领奖台。但如果我能在这里亲自做到，那将是了不起的成就。”
"而一想到如果我真的做到了，我很可能是历史上唯一一位在意大利为法拉利做到这一点的黑人车手，也许吧，所以很多这样的想法都曾在我的脑海中闪过。
刘易斯·汉密尔顿和夏尔·勒克莱尔在米兰受到了热烈欢迎，法拉利车迷聚集在米兰，在House of Peroni Nastro Azzurro 0.0%活动上为这两位F1明星欢呼助威。
"压力很大。你也想为车队拿出好成绩。工厂里有那么多人，他们中的许多人将能来到这场比赛，还有大批涌来的车迷，那种热情是无与伦比的，你也想为他们拿出好的表现。
“我妈妈这周末会来这里，因为我想她还没去过蒙扎，而且还是在法拉利的比赛周末。我想让她体验一下，你也知道，让她把她能带来的所有好运都带来。”
引擎升级无法弥补‘全部差距’
法拉利本赛季第二次引擎升级的到来，应该会提升汉密尔顿争夺胜利的希望。
车队于周三确认，他们已经启用了2026赛季获准的两次引擎改进机会中的第二次。
也许法拉利本赛季最大的弱点就是他们的动力单元比梅赛德斯弱，而梅赛德斯同时也向迈凯伦供应引擎。
汉密尔顿说：“每一点帮助都很重要，我认为直到今年这个时候我们一直在损失，甚至在上站那条如此短的赛道上，整场比赛中我们每圈要损失0.4秒。这是一个巨大的差距，而且我们整个赛季到现在一直背负着这个劣势。
在F1 Show播客节目中，Harry Benjamin认为，尽管结果令人沮丧，汉密尔顿仍然可以从荷兰大奖赛中收获积极的东西。
“我能说的是，当我回到工厂看到每个人都在多么努力地工作时，我真的感到非常自豪。大家都在埋头苦干，每个人都充满热情。
“我看到今年的专注点和去年不一样了。去年，我感觉并没有一个真正的‘北极星’目标。我们尽了最大努力，但并不清楚我们究竟要朝什么方向努力。现在我们有了‘北极星’，我们知道自己需要朝哪个方向前进。
“我认为他们做得非常出色，真正地团结起来并交付了成果。这是向前迈出的一步，虽然还不是我们需要弥补的全部差距，但我们早就知道会是这样。
“但能看到每个周末都有新部件到来、不断改进赛车，看到我们在全力推进，这令人兴奋，我依然坚信我们具备夺冠的实力。”

detailEn: Lewis Hamilton shares thoughts about possibility of becoming first black Ferrari driver to win in Italy ahead of Italian GP

Lewis Hamilton is seeking his first Ferrari victory in Italy this weekend in Monza; Hamilton is hopeful a Ferrari engine upgrade will boost his chances; watch Friday's practice sessions for the Italian GP at 11.30am and 3pm, live on Sky Sports F1
Lewis Hamilton arrived at the Italian GP in a rare Ferrari F40 and revealed that the car's engine bore the same number as his racing number.
Lewis Hamilton says he has been considering the magnitude of potentially becoming the first black Ferrari Formula 1 driver to win a home race for the team, ahead of this weekend's Italian Grand Prix.

The seven-time world champion has enjoyed a much improved second campaign in red, with a maiden Grand Prix victory for the team in Barcelona in June helping to keep him in title contention, as he trails Mercedes' Kimi Antonelli by 59 points with 11 rounds remaining.
Hamilton's hopes of claiming victory in Monza have been boosted by the fact Antonelli will start from the back of the grid as he serves a penalty for exceeding his engine-part allowance.

Asked what a prospective 107th career Grand Prix win would mean to him, Hamilton said: "I've really thought coming into this weekend, as I pondered, just thinking of the sheer magnitude of the concept that I'm coming to this Grand Prix, I didn't even know that I had I was equal with Michael [Schumacher] on [five Monza] wins, for example.
Ferrari's Lewis Hamilton claimed his first win in red at the Barcelona-Catalunya Grand Prix.
"But the thought that there's a first ahead of me, in the sense that potentially, if I was to win, you go into new territory.
"Winning in Monza for the first time with Ferrari is something I've witnessed Charles [Leclerc] win in 2019, when I was on the podium with him. But to do it while I'm here would be phenomenal.

"And the thought of if I did do that, probably I would be the only black driver to ever do that for Ferrari in Italy probably in history, maybe, and so just like a lot of those thoughts have been through my mind.
Lewis Hamilton and Charles Leclerc were greeted with a big reception as Ferrari fans gathered in Milan to cheer on the F1 stars at a House of Peroni Nastro Azzurro 0.0% event.

"The pressure is high. You also want to deliver for the team. There's all those people at the factory, many of them will get to come to this race, the Tifosi, who come in huge numbers and the passion is unmatched, and you want to deliver for them as well.

"And my mum's here this weekend because I don't think she's been to Monza, but also particularly on a Ferrari weekend. I wanted her to experience that and you know bring any of the lucky dust she can bring."
Engine upgrade won't recover 'whole gap'
Hamilton's hopes of victory should be boosted by the arrival of Ferrari's second engine upgrade of the season.
The team confirmed on Wednesday that they have taken up the second of two opportunities they've been granted to improve their engine during their 2026 campaign.
Perhaps Ferrari's biggest weakness this season has been having a weaker power unit than Mercedes, who also supply McLaren with their engines.

Hamilton said: "Every little helps, and I think up until this point of the year we've been losing, even in the last race on such a short circuit we were losing four tenths a lap through the race. That's a huge deficit and we've carried that through the year to this point.
Speaking on the F1 Show podcast, Harry Benjamin believes Lewis Hamilton can take positives away from the Dutch Grand Prix, despite a frustrating result.
"What I can say is I'm really proud when I go back to the factory and see how hard everyone is working. They're really just heads down, and everyone's so enthusiastic.

"I see a different focus this year to last year. Last year, I felt like there wasn't really a north star. We were doing the best we could, but not really knowing exactly what we were trying to aim for. Now we have a north star, and we know where we need to work towards.
"I think they've done a tremendous job to really pull together and deliver. This is a step forward, it's not the whole gap that we need but we knew that would be the case.
"But to see bits coming each weekend, adding to the car, it's exciting to see that we are pushing and I strongly still believe that we've got what it takes to win."

detailEn: United States GP: Lewis Hamilton fastest from Max Verstappen in final practice ahead of Qualifying in Austin

Ferrari's Lewis Hamilton outpaced Red Bull's Max Verstappen in final practice in Austin with Friday's pace-setter Charles Leclerc in third; watch every United States GP session live on Sky Sports F1, with qualifying at 10pm on Saturday and the race at 8pm on Sunday
Lewis Hamilton claims the fastest lap from Max Verstappen in final practice at the United States Grand Prix
Lewis Hamilton topped final practice from Max Verstappen at the United States Grand Prix to set up a tantalising qualifying in Austin.
Hamilton was 0.168s quicker than Verstappen as Ferrari and Red Bull look set to fight for pole position and victory for a second consecutive weekend.
Charles Leclerc topped both of Friday's sessions and had set the quickest time in final practice by one tenth from Hamilton, only for it to be deleted due to track limits.

Leclerc still finished the session in third, ahead of championship leader Kimi Antonelli whose chances of becoming the youngest world champion look extremely difficult, given he must first win the Grand Prix to give himself an opportunity, and Mercedes are a tad off the pace.
Antonelli was three tenths behind Hamilton's pace-setting time with his Mercedes team-mate George Russell in fifth at nearly half a second down.

McLaren's Lando Norris was eighth but would have been in the top five had his best lap not been deleted for track limit, while Oscar Piastri was sixth and Audi's Nico Hulkenberg impressing in seventh.
